annotations.text:
The problem today

Four full-width banners of equal weight before any content. The Excel path (setup, matters once) shouts as loudly as “2 pyramid violations” (a finding, matters now) — and the violations sit fourth. The first layer card is ~500px down, below the fold.

AXIS: compress, don't rethink.

Four banners become one strip of chips; the source drops to a line. Layers rise ~330px.

+ smallest change, nothing moves conceptually
− still a header to read before the subject
− “not measured” still takes a slot to say nothing

AXIS: put findings on the things they are about.

The page is called Testing Layers, so it opens with layers. A violation is about System and Acceptance, so it lives on those two cards — where the red border already was. Unit says its own workbook is missing.

+ no banner duplicates what a card already shows
+ subject is above the fold
− you must scan the grid to count violations

AXIS: the rule is about size, so draw size.

One panel, bars by record count, each row a link. “Acceptance is wider than System” is seen, not read.

+ the strongest at-a-glance read
− Regression (210) dwarfs everything, so 15 vs 13 is invisible in the bars and only the numbers carry it
− two ways to open a layer on one page

AXIS: keep the strip, add the shape.

Option A's chip row stays exactly as it is. Under it the pyramid is drawn to its IDEAL geometry — the trapezoids are the rule, not the data — with each tier carrying its real count and the two broken boundaries labelled 39 ≥ 15 and 15 ≥ 13. Unit is grey because 0 records means the rule cannot be checked, not that it passed.

+ the strip answers “what is wrong” and the shape answers “where”
+ legible at any set of numbers, unlike true-scale widths
− a reader could mistake the ideal shape for the data, which is why every tier is labelled

The alternative, for comparison: widths taken from the real counts. Truthful, and nearly unreadable — Regression is 210 of 277 records, so everything above it is a sliver and the 15-vs-13 violation is two pixels wide.
